subject.title: [Security] Deep code safety scan bypass on symlinks in audit paths

question: Should deep code-safety audit scan only symlink targets contained within the declared audit root, reject all symlinks, or preserve the current skip behavior?
rationale: This choice defines whether audit follows runtime-reachable linked code and whether it is permitted to cross the caller's declared filesystem boundary; source inspection cannot safely infer that product-security policy.

options.title: Bound and report links
options.body: Resolve links, scan only targets contained within the declared root, detect cycles, and report out-of-root or invalid links as audit findings.

options.title: Reject all links
options.body: Treat every symlink under an audited code tree as a security finding without traversing its target, prioritizing a simple fail-closed contract.

options.title: Keep skipping links
options.body: Preserve the existing best-effort scanner behavior and document that symlinked payloads are outside deep code-safety coverage.

recommendation.title: Bound and report links
recommendation.body: Resolve links, scan only targets contained within the declared root, detect cycles, and report out-of-root or invalid links as audit findings.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged and integrated the scanner's original security-audit behavior and are the strongest available owner for its traversal boundary.
